Status: the client’s own description of its processes and key controls, for the walkthroughs

Flow: Project managers commit job costs; vendor invoices arrive at Accounts Payable, are coded to the job and approved by the project manager, and are paid by ACH in a weekly run the Controller approves in the bank portal.
P2P-1 Vendor setup. New vendors and bank account changes are approved by the Controller in the vendor master before the first payment.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: As needed; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The vendor change log
P2P-2 Payment approval. The Controller approves every payment run in the bank portal; the preparer cannot approve; payments of $100,000 or more need the Chief Financial Officer too.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: Weekly; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The bank portal approvals
P2P-3 Invoice approval. The project manager approves each vendor invoice against the job before it is paid.
Owner: Project managers; Frequency: Each invoice; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The approval stamp on the invoice

Flow: Each month the project manager prepares the pay application from the schedule of values; the Controller approves it; the owner pays net of 5% retainage; the Project Accountant posts receipts from the bank.
B2C-1 Pay application approval. Each pay application is approved by the project manager and the Controller before it is sent.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: Monthly, each job; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The pay application log
B2C-2 Cash receipts. Receipts are posted within one business day of the deposit and agreed to the bank.
Owner: Project Accountant; Frequency: Daily; Type: Detective, manual; Evidence: The cash receipts log
Flow: Superintendents approve crew timesheets; the Payroll and HR Manager keeps the employee master and processes payroll biweekly; the Controller approves the register before release.
PAY-1 Rate changes. A pay rate is changed only from a personnel action form signed by the approver.
Owner: Payroll and HR Manager; Frequency: As needed; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The rate change log and the forms
PAY-2 Payroll release. The Controller reviews the payroll register against the prior payroll and approves it before release.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: Biweekly; Type: Detective, manual; Evidence: The payroll approvals log
PAY-3 Leavers. A leaver is paid one final check and inactivated the same day.
Owner: Payroll and HR Manager; Frequency: As needed; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The terminations log
Flow: The Controller closes each month: accruals, depreciation, the job schedule and over and under billings by manual journal entry; the Project Accountant reconciles the bank accounts.
CLS-1 Journal entry review. Manual journal entries over $25,000 are reviewed and initialed by a second person before posting.
Owner: Controller and Chief Financial Officer; Frequency: As needed; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The journal entry listing
CLS-2 Bank reconciliation. The operating account is reconciled within 15 days of month end and reviewed, signed and dated by the Controller.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: Monthly; Type: Detective, manual; Evidence: The signed reconciliation
Flow: The accounting system and the bank portal each assign permissions by user; the Controller administers both.
ITG-1 User access. The Controller assigns system roles so that no one holds two conflicting permissions.
Owner: Controller; Frequency: Annually and on change; Type: Preventive, manual; Evidence: The user access report
Demonstration document. Every name and figure is invented.
